description: Fig. 7 is a single stacked-pattern X-ray diffraction panel for Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe strips rolled at 1050 °C. Intensity (a.u.) is plotted vertically with no printed numeric ticks, against Diffraction angle 2θ (degree) from 20° to 100° with major ticks every 10°. Four vertically offset traces are labelled, bottom to top, 0Be (black), 0.5Be (red), 1.0Be (blue) and 1.5Be (green). A legend keys the phases: γ (red heart), δ (blue diamond), Be11Fe (orange triangle) and Be2Fe (green star). All four traces share the two dominant reflections near 43° ((111), γ) and near 50° ((200), γ), with weaker peaks near 65° ((200), δ), 72–74° ((211) δ and (220) γ), 82° ((112) δ), about 86° ((311) γ) and about 91° ((222) γ). Be additions bring new reflections: 0.5Be shows an orange Be11Fe peak near 86°; 1.0Be adds an orange (011) Be11Fe peak near 49° and a green-star Be2Fe peak near 72°; 1.5Be retains the Be2Fe and Be11Fe peaks, i.e. precipitate peaks grow with Be content.

observations.observation: The panel stacks four XRD traces offset vertically, labelled from bottom to top 0Be (black), 0.5Be (red), 1.0Be (blue) and 1.5Be (green).
Axes are Diffraction angle 2θ (degree) from 20 to 100 (major ticks every 10°) versus Intensity (a.u.) with no printed numeric intensity values.
The legend defines four phase markers: γ (red heart), δ (blue diamond), Be11Fe (orange triangle) and Be2Fe (green star).
All four traces show their two strongest reflections near 43° (labelled (111), γ) and near 50° (labelled (200), γ).
Additional indexed reflections appear near 65° ((200), δ), 72–74° ((211) δ and (220) γ), 82° ((112) δ), about 86° ((311) γ) and about 91° ((222) γ).
An orange Be11Fe marker sits near 86° in the 0.5Be trace, and the 1.0Be trace additionally carries an orange (011) Be11Fe marker near 49° and an orange marker near 86°.
A green-star Be2Fe marker near 72° appears in the 1.0Be and 1.5Be traces but not in the 0Be and 0.5Be traces.
The caption states these are X-ray diffraction patterns of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe strips after rolling at 1050 °C.
The citing text states that with increasing Be content the peaks of the precipitates increase gradually.

The citing text states the 0Be microstructure is austenite and carbide, whereas Be11Fe appears in 0.5Be, Be11Fe and Be2Fe compounds appear in 1.0Be, and Be11Fe, Be12Fe, Be2Fe and Be2C appear in 1.5Be.

The citing text asserts Be12Fe and Be2C precipitates in the 1.5Be steel, but no legend entry or peak label for Be12Fe or Be2C is visible in the figure, which only keys Be11Fe and Be2Fe — the two readings disagree.
The citing text states that no ferrite was observed by XRD when 0.5Be was added to the Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C matrix and that ferrite content increases at 1.0 wt% Be.
Note: the caption text mentions rolling at 1050 °C, but no rolling direction, temperature axis or scale bar appears in this diffraction panel.

subfigures.description: XRD trace of 1.5Be steel; retains the γ/δ reflections at ≈43°, ≈50°, ≈65°, ≈74°, ≈86° and ≈91°, plus an orange Be11Fe triangle peak near 85° and a green-star Be2Fe peak near 72°.
XRD trace of 1.0Be steel; dominant peaks near 43° ((111) γ) and 50° ((200) γ), with a new orange (011) Be11Fe peak near 49°, an orange Be11Fe triangle near 86° and a green-star Be2Fe peak near 72°.
XRD trace of 0.5Be steel; peaks near 43°, 50°, 65°, 74°, 86° and 91°, with one additional orange (Be11Fe) triangle marker near 86° and no clear Be2Fe star.
XRD trace of the Be-free 0Be steel; sharp peaks near 43° ((111) γ) and 50° ((200) γ) plus weaker reflections near 65°, 74°, 86° and 91°, with no orange or green precipitate markers.

unreadable_items: Y-axis (Intensity, a.u.) has no numeric tick values, so peak heights cannot be quantified
Exact 2θ positions of the weaker peaks near 82°, 86° and 91° are only approximate from gridlines
Some peak-index labels overlap stacked traces at the supplied resolution and are only partially readable
